article_type: methodology and comparison guide with worked example
search_intent: Methodology/how-to (which structures exist and how to choose and test one), with secondary comparison intent (feature vs component; team types)
h1: Agile Team Structures: Types, Examples and How to Choose
seo_title: Agile Team Structures: Types, Examples and How to Choose
meta_description: Agile team structures compared: feature, component, platform and enabling teams, how teams interact, reporting lines, scaling, and a worked redesign.
excerpt: How to structure Agile teams across an organisation: team boundary types, composition, interaction modes, line management and multi-team structures, with a decision table and a worked redesign that counts cross-team handoffs before and after.
learning_objectives: Explain the three decisions in an Agile team structure: boundaries, composition and connections
Compare feature/stream-aligned, component, platform, enabling, complicated-subsystem, functional and internal open-source teams
Explain Conway's law, handoff queues and cognitive load as reasons structure matters
Choose interaction modes and a line-management model
Test candidate structures by counting teams touched and handoffs for real upcoming features, and interpret the result
related_npi_course: Sprintcraft: Agile and Scrum Practitioner (named only in the page's existing PMAI box; not mentioned in the body)

external_references.what_it_supports: Conway 1968 quote (Datamation); inverse Conway manoeuvre coined by Jonny LeRoy and Matt Simons in 2010

external_references.what_it_supports: Feature team definition 'long-lived, cross-functional, cross-component'; component-team disadvantages; hybrid models 'drawbacks from both worlds'

external_references.title: PMI Disciplined Agile, How do we organize a large agile team?
external_references.what_it_supports: Component, feature, functional and internal open-source strategies; functional teams add communication overhead and project risk; strategies can be combined

external_references.title: Scaled Agile, Features and Components (updated 17 April 2023)
external_references.what_it_supports: Four team types as template; most teams stream-aligned; no more than 1–3 complicated-subsystem teams per ART; two or three enabling teams across the enterprise common

external_references.title: Mountain Goat Software, Agile Team Structure (updated 31 July 2026)
external_references.what_it_supports: Most teams should be feature teams; conditions for component teams; '20% on five teams' specialist allocation; primary team; do not reorganise constantly

formulas.inputs: 10 illustrative features mapped to W/M/C/D components and to journey teams + platform
formulas.result: Component structure: 30 team touches, average 3.0, 1/10 single-team, 20 handoffs. Feature structure: 11 touches, average 1.1, 9/10 single-team, 1 handoff; reduction 95%

formulas.variables: w assumed average wait per handoff = 5 working days (half a two-week Sprint)
formulas.result: 100 working days total (10.0 per feature) vs 5 (0.5 per feature)
Each team 6; each skill 6; total 24 (matches four component teams of six). Component demand W 9, M 8, C 5 (Buy 4, Account 1), D 8

formula_verification_script:
F=[("Filter search results by size","Browse","WMD",False),
   ("Save basket across devices","Buy","WMCD",False),
   ("Add a digital wallet payment option","Buy","WMC",False),
   ("Export order history","Account","WD",False),
   ("Product recommendation carousel","Browse","WMD",True),
   ("Change delivery address after ordering","Account","WMCD",False),
   ("Fix promotion-code validation","Buy","C",False),
   ("Wish list","Account","WMD",False),
   ("Show stock availability on product pages","Browse","WMD",False),
   ("Guest checkout","Buy","WMCD",False)]
WAIT=5
tc=[];tf=[]
for n,j,c,p in F:
    a=len(c); b=1+p
    tc.append(a); tf.append(b)
    print(f"{n:45s} {j:8s} comp_teams={a} handoffs={a-1} wait={WAIT*(a-1)} | feat_teams={b} handoffs={b-1} wait={WAIT*(b-1)} pairs_comp={a*(a-1)//2}")
N=len(F)
print("avg teams comp",sum(tc)/N,"feat",sum(tf)/N)
print("single-team comp",sum(t==1 for t in tc),"/",N," feat",sum(t==1 for t in tf),"/",N)
hc=sum(t-1 for t in tc); hf=sum(t-1 for t in tf)
print("handoffs comp",hc,"feat",hf,"reduction",(hc-hf)/hc*100)
print("wait days comp",hc*WAIT,"avg",hc*WAIT/N,"feat",hf*WAIT,"avg",hf*WAIT/N)
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(j for _,j,_,_ in F))
print("component load", {k:sum(k in c for _,_,c,_ in F) for k in "WMCD"})
print("pairs comp total",sum(t*(t-1)//2 for t in tc))
print("people",4*6,"new",3*6+6)
alloc={"Browse":dict(W=2,M=2,C=0,D=2),"Buy":dict(W=2,M=1,C=2,D=1),"Account":dict(W=2,M=2,C=1,D=1),"Platform":dict(W=0,M=1,C=3,D=2)}
for t,a in alloc.items(): print(t,sum(a.values()))
print({k:sum(a[k] for a in alloc.values()) for k in "WMCD"}, sum(sum(a.values()) for a in alloc.values()))
print("C features by journey", Counter(j for _,j,c,_ in F if "C" in c))
print("total team touches comp",sum(tc),"feat",sum(tf))
